title: MICE: Multi-animal Interaction Context Encoder — A Hierarchical Foundation Model for Mouse Behavior
claim: A two-stage hierarchical architecture first encodes each entity individually, then fuses entities through a latent bottleneck that scales to any group size.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, stacked stages with dashed pink loss box
description: Two large rounded panels show the two-stage architecture. The left panel, Stage 1 Individual Encoder, takes keypoint trajectories of one mouse over T frames (small mouse sketches at t=1, 2, ..., T). A gray patching block feeds three transformer stages in light, medium and dark blue for local, medium and global attention. Their outputs h(1), h(2) and h(3) go into a tall concatenation bar. Below it, yellow linear layers lead to green HoA (KL) and reconstruction (MSE) loss boxes, each with a white target box. The right panel, Stage 2 Perceiver Social Encoder, takes N animals, each passing through a frozen individual encoder, then a yellow linear projection. A row of orange latent codebook squares feeds a green encode/process/decode block. The output is social embeddings, which go to a dashed purple region for pairwise features, heads and losses.
caption: The MICE architecture. Stage 1 (left, individual encoder): a per-animal pose sequence is tokenized by a patching layer, then processed through three ALBERT-style transformer stages of increasing attention scope (local, medium, global) with weights shared within each stage. Per-stage outputs are concatenated and supervised by three losses: a long-scale Histogram-of-Activities (HoA) loss on Stage 3's output, a short/mid-scale HoA loss on the concatenated output, and a span-masked keypoint reconstruction loss. Stage 2 (right, social encoder): the frozen individual encoder is applied per mouse; per-animal embeddings are fused with raw keypoints and passed to a Perceiver with a learned latent codebook. The latents cross-attend over animals (encode), refine across time (process), and are read back to each animal (decode), producing per-animal social embeddings. Animal pairs are formed by an order-invariant projection and supervised by pairwise HoA and pairwise distance losses.
abstract: Quantifying mouse behavior from pose is a foundational tool in neuroscience, ethology, drug discovery, and animal welfare. Self-supervised foundation models are a natural fit, but a foundation model for mouse behavior must handle social behavior - many behaviors that matter (aggression, courtship, mounting, allogrooming) are inherently multi-animal. Existing self-supervised pose models fall short: they encode each animal independently and discard interaction signal, hard-code the animal count, and pretrain one dataset at a time. We introduce MICE (Multi-animal Interaction Context Encoder), a hierarchical foundation model for mouse behavior that pretrains jointly on six mouse-pose corpora spanning one to four mice and 7 to 27 keypoints. MICE combines a hierarchical individual encoder capturing per-mouse kinematics at multiple temporal scales with a Perceiver-style social encoder whose learned latent codebook decouples parameter count from animal count, so a single checkpoint serves any group size without retraining. Across four evaluation protocols spanning six datasets, MICE matches or exceeds prior keypoint-based baselines, and layer-wise probing shows the social stage incrementally improves discriminability beyond the individual encoder. Code, weights, and data are available at https://github.com/eric0708/MICE.
